name: Forced connections
when: ideas have gone stale and familiar
prompt: Force a collision. How could each of these apply to {subject}?
readback: Most connections are junk; one will be alive. Quote only the alive one and say why it might work.

claims.claim: Exposure to randomly selected stimuli (words or prompts unrelated to the problem) during idea generation increases the number and originality of ideas, compared with generating without stimuli.
claims.construct: random entry / external stimulation in idea generation

claims.claim: Deliberately combining two distant concepts produces more original ideas than working from a single concept, with originality driven by attributes that emerge from the combination.

grounding.helps: when ideas have gone stale and familiar; outside stimuli can lift idea output, but random words themselves are untested, so treat each connection as a prompt to test, not a finding
grounding.backfires: when a stimulus fixes attention on itself instead of widening it, as provided examples do in design studies, and during convergence, where unrelated input is noise
